subject.title: Browser tool: 7 improvements from real-world automation field test

question: Which remaining browser automation slice should OpenClaw own next: model-visible state signals, model-advertised batch actions, CDP element inspection, or post-fill verification?
rationale: The already-merged selector/batch work leaves several meaningful requests, but the next change affects model-facing browser semantics and compatibility with existing ref/snapshot workflows.

options.title: Prioritize state signals
options.body: Scope stale-ref/readiness/CAPTCHA/action-result signals first so agents stop guessing when a new snapshot or human intervention is needed.

options.title: Advertise batch first
options.body: Expose the already-supported batch action shape in the browser tool schema and docs as a narrow follow-up before broader diagnostics.

options.title: Split diagnostics separately
options.body: Track CDP element inspection and post-fill verification as separate product issues with their own safety and proof requirements.

recommendation.title: Prioritize state signals
recommendation.body: Scope stale-ref/readiness/CAPTCHA/action-result signals first so agents stop guessing when a new snapshot or human intervention is needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved work is primarily a product-boundary decision for the bundled browser plugin's model-facing contract.
